mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the corneas, lenses and irises was worthwhile: the planned ray diagrams distinguish bending light from controlling how much enters, then bring both roles together at the retina.

leastWorthwhile.text: Attaching the three clearly labelled fittings was somewhat predictable, even though the resulting comparisons were informative.

surprise.text: The comparison of incoming light with outgoing nerve signals usefully clarified that the eye sends a signal pattern, not a beam of light, to the brain.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the retinal relay’s role was stated more than explained: the descriptions did not show how rods and cones change activity in response to light.

continue.text: I would choose to continue for another chapter: the planned diagrams connected structures to functions clearly, particularly in the focusing sequence, although the mostly obvious fittings offered few difficult decisions.
